issues.title: Show progress while gcmon extract runs
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

gcmon extract prints nothing while it works. On a pyperformance trace it
runs for tens of seconds, and without -v it stays silent even after it
finishes. A run that is working and a run that has hung look the same.

Context

Timed on one machine, on a 29 MB gcmon trace of pyperformance on the
reference branch, which extracts to 205,033 rows:

Stage Time
Read the pyperformance results file 0.04 s
Start the trace processor, load the trace, run the slice query 15.2 s
Read the query's rows into Python 13.0 s
Close the trace processor, resolve each track's process 0.7 s
Match pauses to their processes and benchmarks 4.5 s
Write the CSV 0.9 s
Total 35.7 s
  • The trace processor reports no progress while it loads a trace, so the
    first stage can only say that it is running.
  • The stage that reads rows and the matching stage run in Python, one row
    at a time. The total is not known before the rows are read.
  • Wrote N records to ..., the only line a successful run logs, is at INFO,
    which shows only with -v.
  • Questions the ticket settles: what a run whose stderr is not a terminal
    shows, and whether the closing line shows without -v.

Requirements

  • At a terminal, a run shows which stage it is in from the moment it starts.
  • A stage that runs for seconds shows that it is still advancing.

Constraints

  • The CSV and its .meta.json come out the same as before.
  • The analysis extra stays the only extra extract needs.

Acceptance criteria

  • On a pyperformance trace, gcmon extract run at a terminal shows a
    stage name within a second of starting and keeps showing one until it
    exits.
  • Apart from the trace load, no stage leaves the output unchanged for more
    than a few seconds.
  • The CSV and .meta.json of a trace match those written before the change.
  • CHANGELOG has a line for it.

issues.title: Describe a record's running totals correctly in docs/monitoring.md
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

docs/monitoring.md describes a record's counts as narrower than they are.

  • Its opening says each record describes "what the run freed". The record's
    collected is a running total, not what that run freed.
  • What the counters recover says CPython keeps two cumulative numbers per
    generation, how many runs have finished and how long they took together. A
    record carries five running totals.

Context

  • A record carries collections, collected, uncollectable, candidates
    and duration as running totals, kept per interpreter and generation since
    the interpreter started. heap_size and the timestamps belong to the run
    alone.
  • Both of CPython 3.15's collectors build a record that way, the default
    build's in Python/gc.c and the free-threaded build's in
    Python/gc_free_threading.c, and so does the PEP 848 reference branch.
  • The section's argument uses two of the totals, collections and
    duration, to count the runs gcmon missed and what they cost. That use is
    correct; only the count of totals a record carries is wrong.
  • #230 covers the same facts in docs/formats.md. Its first requirement
    reaches every page under docs/, but its acceptance criteria name only
    docs/formats.md.

Requirements

  • The opening of docs/monitoring.md does not describe a record's counts as
    one run's own.
  • What the counters recover says which running totals a record carries, and
    still says which of them the loss accounting reads.

Constraints

  • A user-facing page carries no CPython internals: the C source files stay
    out of docs/*.md.

Out of scope

  • docs/formats.md, which #230 covers.
  • What a trace or a capture carries.

Acceptance criteria

  • No sentence in docs/monitoring.md describes collected, uncollectable,
    candidates or duration as one run's figure.
  • The number of running totals docs/monitoring.md gives matches the fields a
    record carries as running totals.

issues.title: Name the analysis extra and the extract command where gcmon lists its extras and commands
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

The places that list gcmon's extras and commands predate gcmon extract.

  • The README's Installation section lists the [stats] and [cmdline]
    extras and not [analysis], so a reader of the README cannot learn what
    gcmon extract needs before running it.
  • The same section says each extra degrades gracefully when absent. Without
    [analysis], gcmon extract stops with an error instead.
  • docs/cli.md opens by saying gcmon requires one of three subcommands,
    monitor, run and combine. extract is a fourth.

Context

  • pyproject.toml declares three extras: cmdline (psutil), stats
    (ddsketch) and analysis (perfetto and protobuf).
  • Only gcmon extract needs [analysis]. Without it the command exits
    non-zero with a message naming the extra, and monitor, run and
    combine run as before.
  • The first gcmon extract downloads Perfetto's v58.2 trace processor and
    keeps it for later runs.
  • The extract section of docs/cli.md already documents the command, its
    options and the extra; docs/formats.md documents the table it writes under
    Records table.

Requirements

  • The README's installation section names every extra pyproject.toml
    declares and what each one enables.
  • What the README says about a missing extra is true of each extra it names.
  • The opening of docs/cli.md names every subcommand gcmon has.

Constraints

  • The README links to pages under docs/ by absolute GitHub URL, as its
    existing links do, because PyPI renders it.

Acceptance criteria

  • The README's installation section names [analysis] and the command it
    serves.
  • No sentence in the README says something of every extra that [analysis]
    does not do.
  • The opening of docs/cli.md names monitor, run, combine and
    extract.

issues.title: Fix the pyperformance example in docs/pyperf.md
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

The Usage section of docs/pyperf.md turns the hook on for a pyperformance
run:

gcmon run -o suite.pftrace -m pyperformance run \
    --hook=gcmon --inherit-environ=GCMON_CONTROL_ADDRESS

pyperformance takes no external hook the way pyperf does, so the command
does not mark where each benchmark ran. A reader who follows it expects a
trace whose workers carry marks, and does not get one.

Context

  • pyperformance's run takes --hook, lists its choices from the pyperf
    hooks installed beside pyperformance, and passes it on to each benchmark.
    It runs the benchmark in a virtualenv it builds from pyperf and the
    benchmark's own requirements.
  • In that virtualenv, pyperf's Runner takes its --hook choices from the
    entry points installed there. gcmon is not among them, so the benchmark's
    pyperf rejects --hook=gcmon.
  • Both points are read from the source of pyperformance 1.14.0 and pyperf
    2.10.0.
  • #228 joins a pyperformance worker to its benchmark through the worker's
    command line for the same reason.

Requirements

  • Every command docs/pyperf.md shows runs as written.
  • The page says the hook does not reach pyperformance's benchmarks.

Constraints

  • The examples that drive pyperf directly, gcmon run -s my_benchmark.py and
    gcmon run -m pyperf timeit, stay.

Out of scope

  • Making the hook work under pyperformance.

Acceptance criteria

  • No command in docs/pyperf.md turns the hook on for a pyperformance run.
  • docs/pyperf.md says a pyperformance run gets no marks from the hook.

issues.title: Document collected, uncollectable, candidates and duration as running totals
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

docs/formats.md describes collected, uncollectable, candidates and
duration as figures of one GC run. A record carries each as a running
total, kept per interpreter and generation since the interpreter started, and
gcmon writes it as read. A reader who sums collected over a capture's
records, or reads the G0 collected counter as what each run freed, gets a
wrong number.

Context

  • CPython's add_stats in Python/gc.c builds each record from a copy of the
    generation's previous one: it adds one to collections and the run's own
    figures to collected, uncollectable, candidates and duration.
    heap_size, ts_start and ts_stop belong to the run alone. CPython 3.15
    and the PEP 848 reference branch agree.
  • In docs/formats.md:
    • The JSONL field table gives collected as "Objects this run collected",
      uncollectable as "Objects that could not be collected", candidates as
      "Candidate objects for collection" and duration as "Pause duration in
      seconds". Only collections is called cumulative.
    • Both example lines under JSONL output carry a duration equal to
      ts_stop - ts_start, which only one run's figure would.
    • The GC Pause(gen) slice carries "that run's counters as args", and the
      G{gen} counter tracks carry the four fields. Neither says they are
      running totals, and each counter track rises over an interpreter's life.
  • docs/internals/gc-record-clock.md already calls the duration gcmon reads
    cumulative.

Requirements

  • Every page under docs/ that describes the four fields says they are
    running totals since the interpreter started.
  • docs/formats.md says how a reader gets one run's figure from them, and
    what the difference covers when records were lost between two.
  • The JSONL example lines agree with the table.

Constraints

  • A user-facing page carries no CPython internals: add_stats stays out of
    docs/*.md.

Out of scope

  • Changing what a trace or a capture carries.

Acceptance criteria

  • No page under docs/ describes collected, uncollectable, candidates
    or duration as one run's figure.
  • In docs/formats.md, the JSONL table, its example lines, the
    GC Pause(gen) slice and the counter tracks describe the four as running
    totals.

issues.title: Check documentation links in CI
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Part of #149, and needs nothing from it.

Problem

Nothing checks that the links in the documentation still resolve. Every
relative link in the 78 markdown files resolves today, and all 43 external
URLs answer, so nothing here is a repair. The job holds that state against
the next rename or the next dead upstream.

Context

Links run across the whole tree, not only docs/. README.md,
CONTRIBUTING.md, specs/ and the ADRs all carry them, and 22 links leave
docs/ for most of those.

Open questions this ticket settles:

  • The checker. lycheeverse/lychee-action is the obvious candidate and
    nothing here depends on it being the one.
  • Whether URLs inside fenced code blocks are checked. docs/cli.md and
    docs/perfetto-sql.md carry URLs in examples, and both readings are
    defensible.
  • Whether to run on a schedule as well as on push. An external link can rot
    with no commit touching it. Against that: a scheduled failure caused by
    someone else's outage teaches people to ignore a red mark, so a green
    history first is worth arguing about.

Requirements

  • Check relative links and external URLs across the whole tree.
  • Fail a pull request that breaks one.
  • Report how many links were checked.

Constraints

  • .github/zizmor.yml requires every uses: pinned by commit.
  • The tree carries many github.com links. An unauthenticated checker will
    meet the rate limit; the workflow token lifts it.
  • Anything that has to be skipped needs the reason recorded next to it, not
    a bare pattern.

Out of scope

Fixing links, because there are none to fix. If the first run disagrees, the
fix belongs in the same pull request with a line saying what moved.

Acceptance criteria

  • the job passes on main as it stands
  • a pull request adding a link to a file that does not exist fails it
  • a pull request adding a URL that 404s fails it
  • the run reports how many links it checked
  • the job finishes in a time that does not make people dread it, and the
    pull request says what that was

issues.title: Publish the documentation to GitHub Pages
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Part of #149. Needs #150.

Problem

#150 builds a site into a directory. Nothing serves it.

Context

pyproject.toml points Documentation at
https://github.com/sergey-miryanov/gcmon/blob/main/docs/README.md, and
README.md and docs/README.md name the documentation by file path. Once a
site exists, all three have a better target.

ci.yml already runs on push and pull_request and holds seven jobs, each
checking out with persist-credentials: false and then using the local
./.github/actions/setup, which installs Poetry and the dependencies.

Open questions this ticket settles:

  • Deploy from a workflow artifact or from a branch.
  • Whether a pull request gets a preview build, and whether it deploys
    anywhere. A preview deployment costs a token with write scope, which makes
    it a decision and not a detail.
  • Whether the docs build gets its own workflow or a job in ci.yml.

Requirements

  • Publish on push to main.
  • Serve at a stable URL.
  • Fail the run, and publish nothing, when the build fails.
  • Point pyproject.toml and the READMEs at the site, in this pull request or
    a named later one.

Constraints

  • The Pages source has to be switched to GitHub Actions in repository
    settings. That one is the owner's; a workflow cannot do it.
  • .github/zizmor.yml sets unpinned-uses to ref-pin, so every uses: is
    pinned by commit with the tag in a trailing comment. Existing workflows
    show the shape.
  • Two pushes to main in quick succession must not race each other to
    publish.

Out of scope

Versioned documentation, one set per release. A custom domain.

Acceptance criteria

  • a push to main publishes the site, and the URL serves the index built
    from README.md
  • a build failure leaves the previous site standing
  • every uses: is pinned by commit, and zizmor passes
  • the URL is recorded somewhere a reader will find it

issues.title: Add a documentation build
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Part of #149. Publishing is #151, link checking is #152.

Problem

gcmon has 78 markdown files and no documentation build.

Context

docs/ holds four readers: operators (docs/*.md, 10 files), the design
record (docs/adr/, 29), CPython background (docs/internals/, 1), and
agents working in this repo (docs/agents/, 4). specs/ holds work that is
specified and not built. README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md
sit outside docs/.

#149 measured the following on this tree. They constrain a build; they do
not pick one.

  • 22 relative links leave docs/. A build rooted at docs/ breaks all 22.

  • MkDocs refuses to root a build at the directory holding its own config:

    ERROR - Config value 'docs_dir': The 'docs_dir' should not be the parent
        directory of the config file.

    The mkdocs-same-dir plugin removes that restriction. Another builder will
    have its own answer, or no such restriction.

  • A builder rooted at the repository copies what it finds. MkDocs put 164
    .py, .toml and .lock files into the output before the config
    excluded them.

  • Dropping a markdown tree from the build costs the links pointing into it.
    specs/ costs 12, docs/agents/ costs 3. MkDocs reports those at INFO,
    which its --strict does not fail on.

Which of those trees belong on a page aimed at someone running gcmon is the
open question. Three ways to treat the ones that do not:

  1. Build them and keep them out of the navigation.
  2. Leave them out of the build and accept 15 dead links.
  3. Leave them out and rewrite those 15 links to absolute GitHub URLs.

On the choice of builder: MkDocs 1.6.1 is the current release, from August
2024. Material for MkDocs pins mkdocs<2,>=1.6 and prints a build-time
warning that MkDocs 2.0 drops the plugin system and the theming system with
no migration path. ProperDocs 1.6.7 continues MkDocs 1.x. #149 rejects
Sphinx with MyST on the grounds that the API reference it would earn covers
six symbols. A pull request that picks something else and meets the
acceptance criteria is a fine outcome. Say what it weighed.

Requirements

  • Turn every page under docs/, plus README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and
    CHANGELOG.md, into a static site.
  • Leave every relative link that resolves on GitHub resolving in the site.
  • Ship no source file.
  • Build from one command, which #151 can call from CI.
  • Decide what happens to specs/ and docs/agents/, and record the
    reasoning.

Constraints

  • Two links point into .github/, from CONTRIBUTING.md and
    docs/RELEASE.md. MkDocs skips a directory whose name starts with a dot,
    and a builder that does the same will not resolve them.
  • The docs dependencies want their own Poetry group.
    .github/actions/setup already installs with --all-groups --all-extras,
    which is also the command CONTRIBUTING.md opens with.
  • If #137 has landed, the build command belongs in the justfile.
  • The stack installs into a Python 3.15 venv.

Out of scope

Publishing. Link checking. What any page says, beyond the links the decision
above forces.

Acceptance criteria

  • one command builds the site, and treats a warning as a failure
  • the index comes from README.md
  • the guide pages, the ADR index and CONTRIBUTING.md are reachable by
    navigation
  • no .py, .toml or .lock file in the output
  • the output directory is gitignored
  • the pull request states which of the three options it took for specs/
    and docs/agents/, and what became of those 15 links

issues.title: Publish the documentation as a site
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

78 markdown files, 44 of them under docs/, and no build. GitHub renders
them. There is no search, no navigation, and no address for a page that is
not a file path.

Context

docs/ holds four readers in one directory:

Tree Files Reader
docs/*.md 10 operators driving gcmon
docs/adr/ 29 why the design has this shape
docs/internals/ 1 CPython background under the design
docs/agents/ 4 agents working in this repo

README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md and specs/ sit outside
docs/ and are linked from inside it.

22 relative links leave docs/. Setting a build's root to docs/ breaks all
of them, and MkDocs refuses to root a build at the directory holding its own
config:

ERROR - Config value 'docs_dir': The 'docs_dir' should not be the parent
        directory of the config file.

mkdocs-same-dir removes that restriction. Under it, over this tree,
mkdocs build --strict exits 0 with no warnings and README.md becomes the
index.

A builder rooted at the repository copies what it finds: MkDocs put 164
.py, .toml and .lock files into the output before the config excluded
them.

Dropping a markdown tree from the build costs the links pointing into it, and
MkDocs reports those at INFO, which --strict does not fail on. They resolve
on GitHub and 404 for a site reader.

Dropped Links lost
specs/ 12
docs/agents/ 3

A third route exists: MkDocs builds a page whether or not nav names it, so
a tree can be built and left out of the navigation. #150 carries that choice
and states the three options.

Two further links, from CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/RELEASE.md, point into
.github/. MkDocs skips a directory whose name starts with a dot.

MkDocs 1.6.1 is the current release, from August 2024. Material for MkDocs
9.7.7 pins mkdocs<2,>=1.6 and prints a build-time warning that MkDocs 2.0
drops the plugin system and the theming system with no migration path.
ProperDocs 1.6.7 continues MkDocs 1.x. Which of those to build on, or whether
to leave the family, is #150's to settle.

Requirements

  • A published site covering the pages a reader running gcmon needs.
  • Every relative link that resolves on GitHub resolves in the site, or the
    ticket that breaks it says what it did instead.
  • A build that runs locally and in CI from the same command.

Constraints

  • .github/zizmor.yml requires every workflow uses: pinned by commit.
  • Turning on Pages is a repository setting, not something a workflow can do.
  • gcmon targets Python 3.15, and the docs stack installs into that venv.

Rejected

  • Sphinx with MyST. The case for it is an API reference. __all__ names
    six symbols and one page shows a Python import.
  • Pages serving docs/ under a Jekyll theme. No build config, and only
    docs/ publishes. Every ../ link 404s.
  • No site at all. Nothing is broken today: every relative link in the
    tree resolves and all 43 external URLs answer. Under this reading #152
    still stands.

Acceptance criteria

  • #150 add the build
  • #151 publish it to Pages (needs #150)
  • #152 check the links, which needs neither

issues.title: How to use gcmon pausing with loss handling
issues.author: sergey-miryanov

issues.title: Extract a trace's records into a CSV file
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

A trace holds every record gcmon read from a pyperformance run, but nothing
in gcmon writes those records out as a table another tool can load. Reading
them takes Perfetto's trace processor and SQL against gcmon's track layout.

pep848-sim needs them as a table (sergey-miryanov/pep848-sim#117). Its
presets model pyperformance benchmarks, and a test holds each preset's
yield, collected over candidates, to its benchmark's, per collector,
generation and kind of collection. The targets come from gcmon traces of
pyperformance on the PEP 848 reference branch, loaded from files that a
fresh trace replaces, so no figure from a trace gets typed into that repo.

Context

Read by SQL from a gcmon trace of pyperformance on the reference branch, 160
workers once the six calibration workers are left out:

Benchmark gen 0 gen 1 gc.collect(), gen 2
create_gc_cycles 0 candidates 0 candidates 22.1%, 20,488 runs
json_loads 0 candidates 0 candidates 26.1%, 10 runs
async_tree_io_tg 0.01% 0.00% 35.2%, 15 runs
connected_components 0.03% 0.00% 97.4%, 25 runs
  • gc.collect() frees most of each benchmark's cyclic garbage. Only
    create_gc_cycles calls it itself; the rest come from pyperf or from the
    interpreter shutting down. pep848-sim takes each worker whole, start-up and
    shutdown included: it models the worker's object graph and how the
    collector processes it, so the table needs no split between a benchmark's
    timed part and the rest.
  • collections, candidates and collected are lifetime totals per
    interpreter and generation. Gaps in collections show lost records, and a
    lost record's counts fold into the next one read.
  • pyperformance takes no external hook the way pyperf's --hook does, so
    gcmon's pyperf hook does not run in its workers and a pyperformance trace
    carries no marks. gcmon-results' prepare already joins each worker to its
    benchmark in _group_pyperformance_workers: it reads the bm_* script, the
    arguments after it, --worker-task and --calibrate-loops from the
    worker's command line, and matches them against pyperformance's results
    JSON. pyperf starts separate workers for each benchmark a script runs, and
    --worker-task says which: bm_xml_etree's workers split 21 to a task
    across tasks 0 to 3, one task per XML benchmark.
  • On the same trace, prepare matched 70 workers to 54 of the results' 119
    benchmarks and listed the rest as missing, async_tree_io_tg among them.
  • Perfetto's Python API launched a v57 trace_processor_shell, which read the
    trace's zstd batches as an empty trace with no error. A v58.2 binary read
    it in full.
  • gcmon-results prepare selects gc.% slice names and extracted no slices
    from the same trace.
  • A trace records neither the build nor the thresholds, and spec 0020, which
    would add both, needs a change on CPython's side. The build does not: gcmon
    and its target run the same CPython version, so gcmon names the build from
    its own interpreter.

Requirements

  • One row per record in the trace, carrying these fields under the names a
    record gives them:

    Field What pep848-sim reads from it
    benchmark which benchmark the record ran in
    the worker's pid and pid epoch which worker a row belongs to
    iid which of the worker's interpreters a row continues
    whether the worker calibrates calibration workers are left out
    ts the order of a worker's records
    generation, auto_collect the kind of collection
    collections, candidates, collected lifetime totals, as read
    heap_size, heap_size_stop how large the heap was around the run
    old_work, survivor_count the incremental collector's budget and survivors, empty on a stock build
    increment_size how far the object graph's links reach in an old collection's increment

  • A record's benchmark is the name pyperformance's results JSON gives the
    benchmark its worker ran.

  • Only the benchmarks named can be kept, so the files stay small enough to
    commit.

  • Beside the table, the run it came from: the build's commit, the collector
    (-X gc=legacy or not), the thresholds, gcmon's and pyperformance's
    versions, the date and the trace's hash. What neither the trace nor
    pyperf's JSON holds can be given on the command line.

Constraints

  • It reads the traces gcmon 0.9.1 writes, zstd batches included.
  • Python's standard csv module reads the table, and a header row names the
    fields: pep848-sim's loader takes no third-party package.
  • The counters stay lifetime totals as read. The reader takes the differences,
    which keeps a lost record's counts in the totals.

Out of scope

  • Running pyperformance again under gcmon: pep848-sim#117 does that.
  • Anything the table feeds, such as yields or plots.
  • A GC run's reason, which records do not carry yet: #229. Once both land,
    the table carries it like any other field.

Acceptance criteria

  • On a gcmon trace of pyperformance, with calibration workers left out, each
    benchmark's rows end with the lifetime totals that SQL reads from the last
    pause spans of that benchmark's workers.
  • On such a trace, xml_etree_parse's rows come from its own workers, apart
    from the other three XML benchmarks', and every async_tree_io_tg worker
    has rows.
  • Keeping one benchmark leaves only its rows.
  • docs/cli.md and docs/formats.md describe the command and the table's
    fields, and CHANGELOG has a line for it.

issues.title: Add --basetemp=.temp to the architecture test run
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

The architecture job's Check the layers step runs
poetry run pytest -m architecture. Every other pytest command in ci.yml
pins --basetemp=.temp. The architecture recipe in the justfile from #137
copies the CI command, so the gap is in both files.

Change

Add --basetemp=.temp to that command, in .github/workflows/ci.yml and in
the justfile. Needs #137 for the justfile half.

Acceptance criteria

  • Both commands read poetry run pytest --basetemp=.temp -m architecture.
  • CI is green.

issues.title: just changelog with no tag previews the last released section, not WIP
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Problem

just changelog with no tag prints the section for the version in
pyproject.toml. Between releases that version is the one already published,
so the recipe prints release notes that shipped weeks ago and never shows the
## WIP block where the unreleased entries accumulate. It exits 0, so nothing
says the output is stale.

Today, with version = "0.6.0" in pyproject.toml, just changelog prints
the ## Version 0.6.0 (2026-08-21) section. The ## WIP block above it, the
one every merged PR has been adding to since, is unreachable from the recipe.

Context

  • The recipe is changelog tag="" in the justfile; it passes the argument
    through to .github/scripts/extract_changelog.py, whose resolve_version
    falls back to tool.poetry.version when no tag is given.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md tells a contributor to add their entry under ## WIP, and
    docs/RELEASE.md has the release bump the version and open a
    ## Version X.Y.Z section below ## WIP. So the pyproject version names
    the WIP block only during a release PR, after the bump.
  • The Extract changelog step in .github/workflows/release.yml always
    passes an explicit "$TAG", so the release path never takes the fallback.
  • docs/RELEASE.md documents the no-tag form under Preview the changelog as
    "uses pyproject.toml version", and that text describes the behaviour this
    issue is asking to change.
  • tests/test_extract_changelog.py covers the script, loading it by path and
    swapping CHANGELOG_PATH and PYPROJECT_PATH around each call. Six of its
    cases pin the no-tag fallback and will read differently after this change:
    test_falls_back_to_pyproject_when_tag_missing and
    test_falls_back_to_pyproject_when_tag_lacks_v_prefix,
    test_prints_body_and_exits_zero, and the three
    TestMainWritesToGitHubOutput cases that run with no tag and assert the
    0.2.0 body.
  • That file's fixture changelog already carries a ## WIP block, and no test
    asserts against it today.
  • Nothing exercises the justfile recipe; the tests reach the script directly.

Requirements

  • just changelog with no argument shows the changes accumulated for the next
    release, not the last released section.
  • just changelog vX.Y.Z and just changelog X.Y.Z keep printing that
    version's section.
  • A requested section that does not exist stays an error: a message naming the
    headers that were found, and a non-zero exit.

Constraints

  • The release workflow consumes the script's stdout and its body write to
    $GITHUB_OUTPUT; both keep their current shape.
  • The script stays standard library only and keeps running under the Python
    the release workflow sets up.
  • A justfile recipe stays a single command with no shell-specific syntax, so
    it works under both PowerShell and sh.
  • ## WIP is the heading the rest of the repo already writes; renaming it is
    not part of this.

Out of scope

The release PR flow. Once the version is bumped and the ## Version X.Y.Z
section is open, previewing the release body by tag is enough.

Acceptance criteria

  • On main as it stands, just changelog prints the ## WIP body.
  • just changelog v0.6.0 prints the ## Version 0.6.0 body, unchanged.
  • Asking for a version with no section fails, with the found headers named.
  • docs/RELEASE.md describes what the no-tag form does.

issues.title: Delete the Makefile and document just in the contributing guide
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Part of #135, and the last of them. Blocked by #138 and #139. The
Makefile stays until every workflow is proven to be running on recipes.

Problem

Makefile is referenced by no workflow, no document and no pre-commit hook.
CONTRIBUTING.md spells every command out by hand, which is the second copy
#135 exists to remove.

Context

By the time this lands, the Makefile's six targets are all accounted for:
test, build and the two typecheck-* targets became recipes in #137,
help became just --list, and install became
poetry install --all-groups --all-extras, the same command
.github/actions/setup runs, replacing a pip install -e . that was wrong
for a Poetry project.

The guide says poetry run just because it is correct from any shell and on
a fresh clone, and it is what the workflows run. The activated-venv shorthand
is mentioned second, depending as it does on a step the reader has to have
taken.

Requirements

1. Delete Makefile. Every occurrence of "make" under docs/ and
specs/ is the English verb. Confirm with grep -rn "Makefile" . before
removing it, and grep -rn "make " .github/ after.

2. CONTRIBUTING.md, where each command becomes its recipe:

Written today Becomes
poetry run pytest poetry run just test
poetry run pytest -m stress poetry run just stress
poetry run pytest -m fuzz poetry run just fuzz
poetry run pytest -m architecture poetry run just architecture
poetry run pytest tests/benchmarks -m benchmark --codspeed poetry run just bench
poetry run mypy src tests and poetry run pyrefly check src tests one poetry run just typecheck
poetry run ruff check src poetry run just lint
python .github/scripts/wrap_markdown.py <paths> poetry run just wrap <paths>

just wrap --check docs/cli.md works too: wrap takes +paths and expands
it unquoted, and --check reaches the script as its flag.

Constraints

  • Leave the first two commands alone. CONTRIBUTING.md opens with
    poetry install --all-groups --all-extras and
    poetry run pre-commit install, and the first of those is what puts just
    in the venv. Turning it into just install would tell a reader with a
    fresh clone to run a command that does not exist yet.
  • Keep Markdown wrapped at 78 columns, as the file already is.

Out of scope

README.md needs no change: its ## Contributing section links the
contributing guide and carries no commands of its own, which is the point of
routing this here. No new documentation page either, since just --list
prints each recipe's description and writing the commands out again in prose
would create the second copy #135 exists to remove. No CHANGELOG entry: the
standing ### Internal line under ## WIP covers it, and no user-facing
behaviour changes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Makefile is gone and grep -rn "Makefile" . finds nothing outside .git
  • CI green on all three operating systems
  • grep -nE "poetry run (pytest|mypy|pyrefly|ruff)" CONTRIBUTING.md finds
    nothing, and neither does grep -n "wrap_markdown" CONTRIBUTING.md
  • following CONTRIBUTING.md from a fresh clone, meaning
    poetry install --all-groups --all-extras and then the recipes, gets you
    to a working test run
  • python .github/scripts/wrap_markdown.py --check CONTRIBUTING.md reports
    it already wrapped

issues.title: Require a subcommand in the CLI parser
issues.author: sergey-miryanov
issues.bodyHTML:
Part of #142.

gcmon with no subcommand prints an AttributeError traceback, and
gcmon 12345 exits 2 with an invalid-choice message. The parser should
require a subcommand, which turns both into one usage message, and the dead
fallback code in main goes with it. #142 has the reasoning and the two
alternatives that were rejected.

Everything here is in src/gcmon/cli/main.py. Line numbers are as of writing.

1. Make the subcommand mandatory

In _create_parser (line 52):

subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", help="Available commands")

becomes

subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True, help="Available commands")

2. Delete the dead code in main

Lines 143-153 today:

    # Dispatch via args.func (set by each subparser's set_defaults)
    if hasattr(args, "func"):
        return int(args.func(args))

    # No command specified: default to monitor
    if args.command is None:
        return main(["monitor", *argv])

    # Unknown command (should not happen due to argparse)
    logger.error("Unknown command: %s", args.command)
    return 1

become:

    # Dispatch via args.func (set by each subparser's set_defaults)
    return int(args.func(args))

All three subparsers call set_defaults(func=...) (monitor_cmd.py:30,
convert_cmd.py:68, run_cmd.py:45), so once the subcommand is required,
args.func always exists. Keep the hasattr guard and mypy strict will
object that main can fall off the end without returning an int, so the
guard has to go with the branches it was guarding.

Deleting the logger.error line leaves the module-level logger at
main.py:16 unused; remove that too. The logging import stays, because
_setup_logging binds its own local logger.

3. Tests, in tests/test_cli.py

  • main([]) raises SystemExit with code == 2, and the usage message names
    the three subcommands.
  • main(["12345"]), the form the README's Quick Start prints today, raises
    SystemExit with code == 2.
  • Regression: monitor, run and combine still dispatch.
  • Regression: --version still exits 0. It is a top-level action that fires
    during parsing, so it exits before argparse checks the new requirement —
    worth pinning, because it is the one top-level invocation that must survive.

Prior art in the same file: test_main_combine_command for dispatch through
main, and TestCliHelp for a parser that exits.

Assert the exit status the operator sees rather than reading main's source
to prove the branch is gone; the second proves the code changed and not what
it does.

4. CHANGELOG

One line under ## WIP → ### Bugfixes:

gcmon with no subcommand prints a usage message and exits 2, where it used
to print an AttributeError traceback

Not ### Breaking changes: nothing that worked stops working. gcmon 12345
exits 2 before this change and after it.

Out of scope

The documented examples that omit the subcommand. Nine of them across
README.md, docs/cli.md and docs/rss.md are #144, and this ticket does
not touch documentation.

Acceptance

  • python -m gcmon exits 2 with error: the following arguments are required: command
  • python -m gcmon 12345 exits 2 with the invalid-choice message it prints today
  • python -m gcmon --version exits 0
  • poetry run pytest passes, including the four cases above
  • poetry run ruff check src, poetry run mypy src tests and
    poetry run pyrefly check src tests are clean

sergey-miryanov/pep848-sim#117.title: Load the benchmarks' collections from gcmon's CSV
sergey-miryanov/pep848-sim#117.author: sergey-miryanov
sergey-miryanov/pep848-sim#117.bodyHTML:
Each preset is checked by yield against its benchmark: collected over candidates, which leaves scale out. gcmon traces pyperformance's workers and records every collection with the runtime's counters, so the targets come from its traces. No number from a trace is typed into the repo: a fresh trace, loaded again, moves every target.

The change

  • gcmon extracts a trace into a CSV file, one row per collection, with the columns below, and a metadata file beside it (sergey-miryanov/gcmon#228).
  • A loader in tools/ reads those files and gives each benchmark, per collector and generation, the collections, candidates, collected and yield of its automatic collections, and of the gc.collect() calls it makes before shutdown. The tests read it; sim.zip never ships it.
  • Rerun pyperformance under gcmon's latest version on the reference branch, sergey-miryanov/cpython@incremental-gc-update-2, at a commit the metadata records: once with the incremental collector and once with -X gc=legacy. Done on 2026-10-26 at revision 5542f2021c2: pp-inc.csv and pp-legacy.csv, each with its .meta.json.
  • The CSV and metadata files from the rerun live in the repo under data/, as gcmon wrote them. The mock files and tools/mock_data.py go.
  • The loader takes each worker whole up to shutdown: interpreter start-up, imports, the benchmark's loops and pyperf's bookkeeping alike. pyperformance's benchmarks are no GC benchmarks, and their timed part means nothing to the collector, so a preset models a worker's object graph and how the collector processes it, never one part of the worker.
  • A collection is explicit when its auto_collect is 0, whoever started it: the benchmark, pyperf or the interpreter shutting down.
  • Shutdown's collections set no target, in the loader or in the simulator's tally. gcmon reads a process from outside, once a tick, and a process can exit before the next tick. Shutdown's rows come last, so a lost one has no later row to fold into: in the rerun, most workers lack at least one of their three.
  • The loader leaves out pyperf's calibration workers and the processes with no benchmark name, which are not workers.
  • The yield test runs. The presets whose yields still miss their benchmark's fail it as strict xfails, each naming the issue that fits it: create_gc_cycles under both collectors (#118), json_loads under the legacy one (#119), xml_etree_parse under both (#120) and connected_components under the incremental one (#122).

Settled

Shutdown's first collection. finalize_modules' two collections carry reason 1, and _Py_Finalize's carries 2, as a gc.collect() call does. The loader takes a worker's last reason-2 row for shutdown's, unless an automatic collection follows it. In the rerun no automatic collection follows any worker's last reason-2 row.

  • Of the five benchmarks, only create_gc_cycles calls gc.collect(): 1,024 times a worker under the incremental collector and 512 under the legacy one, since pyperf calibrated 128 loops a value against 64. In the other four, every reason-2 row is shutdown's, and the rule leaves them no explicit target.
  • Where gcmon lost all three of shutdown's rows, the rule leaves out the benchmark's last call instead: 11 of create_gc_cycles' 20 workers under the incremental collector, 15 under the legacy one. Its yield moves by under 0.01 points: 22.0747% against 22.0833%.
  • An exact rule would need gcmon to read the interpreter's finalizing flag at each collection.

The tolerance. A preset's yield passes within a fifth of its benchmark's or half a point of the objects examined, whichever is wider. A benchmark's 20 workers agree to within 0.01 points, so their spread cannot set it. Most targets sit at 0.05% or under, where a share of the target leaves no room, and half a point keeps a preset that finds no garbage apart from a benchmark whose collections find 1.4%. The old 5 points was wider than every target but one.

Columns

Needed:

Column What it holds
benchmark pyperformance's name for it, such as json_loads or xml_etree_parse
pid, pid_epoch the process: with benchmark, they name one worker in the file
calibration 1 for pyperf's calibration workers, which the loader leaves out
ts when the collection started, in ns, to order a worker's rows
generation 0, 1 or 2, as the runtime files it
auto_collect 1 for a collection the runtime started on its own, 0 for gc.collect() and for shutdown's
reason the branch's _PyGC_Reason: 0 for heap, 1 for shutdown, 2 for manual (sergey-miryanov/gcmon#229). Shutdown runs three full collections: PyGC_Collect() in _Py_Finalize, which carries 2, then finalize_modules' two, which carry 1
collections, candidates, collected the runtime's running totals for the worker and generation, as read; the loader takes differences, and a row gcmon lost folds into the next one it read, except a worker's last, which has none to fold into

Wanted:

Column What it gives us
heap_size, heap_size_stop objects in the heap before and after: how large each structure is beside the rest
old_work the work budget, to hold the incremental collector's budget against the simulator's
increment_size objects in each increment an old collection forms: how far the object graph's links reach
survivor_count survivors of the collection

No column gives the allocation clock. CPython's allocator does not report the bytes it has allocated, and RSS samples cannot stand in for them, so a preset's length still comes from its automatic collections, each threshold0 kB after the last (ADR 0011).

Metadata: the trace and its hash, the Python build with its revision, pyperformance's and pyperf's versions, and the date. The collector and the thresholds come as columns, gc_type (1 legacy, 2 incremental) and threshold0 to threshold2. The loader skips gcmon's version.

Done when

  • The loader reads the rerun's files and gives each of the five benchmarks its yield per collector and generation, for its automatic collections and for its gc.collect() calls before shutdown, the yield test runs with the unfitted presets as strict xfails, and just check passes.
